mechanism_narrative: A higher level of non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates stronger labor market conditions, which support consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS is above its 12-month moving average, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 6.5% indicates a tightening labor market, which typically leads to higher consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE is below 6.5%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in industrial production (INDPRO) and decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a robust economic expansion that accelerates corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The effect is multiplicative: the return impact is significantly larger when both indicators move in the expected direction than when only one does.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO rises and UNRATE falls, or the interaction term's coefficient in a regression is not statistically significant (p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary easing cycles (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%), a rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a strengthening economy that benefits from low interest rates, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.5% and INDPRO rises (current value > previous month's value), or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 0.25% indicates the start of a monetary tightening cycle, which increases the cost of capital and dampens equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 0.25%, or the Rank IC falls below -0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong demand for residential construction, which typically leads to increased economic activity and corporate profits, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST is above its 12-month moving average, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer demand, which accelerates corporate earnings growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The effect is non-additive: the return impact is significantly larger when both indicators move upward than when only one does.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST rises and RSAFS rises, or the interaction term's coefficient in a regression is not statistically significant (p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply-expansion phase (INDPRO > 100), a rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates sustained economic growth that supports corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO > 100 and INDPRO rises (current value > previous month's value), or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
